reachable: Yes, at the scored position specifically. to_obs is an unconditional matmul applied to the read-position prediction in cups_probe (lines 275, 405, 609) via the deepcopied net.target_module (eval/adapter.py:197-198); it takes no z_prev dependence and no observation-present gate, so it cannot switch off at the read whose observation is withheld. The map is demonstrably non-identity long before scoring: in a real harness._train run the first rebuild lands at exactly step 192 (warmup_accum 48 x accum_every 4, confirmed — _observe_pairs succeeded on every one of 250 attempts over 1000 steps on realistic data), i.e. 4.8% of the 4000-step default budget, so failure-mode 3 in the hypothesis does not bite. Gradient: the module holds buffers only and has no parameters to train (verified — register_buffer x4, no register_parameter, so the optim's key-shape router and its (D,D) spectral cap genuinely see nothing new, as claimed); the mechanism acts by re-metricizing every distance term in the loss from step 192 onward, which reaches the whole trunk. The estimator itself is faithful to its description: trace(contrast) = 1.0000 maintained; the trace-renormalize-then-shrink and the mean(lam^p)=1 rescale are exactly as described (mean f^2 = 0.99999999939); fwd and inv are mutually exact by eigenvalue construction (max|fwd@inv - I| = 9.1e-8, i.e. float32 round-off, not an iterative approximation); the eigh costs 35-44 ms per rebuild, one per 80 steps — negligible, and the author correctly flagged that estimate as unmeasured. Both prunes were verified by ablation to matter as claimed: dropping the rank prune lets the silent-vs-content direction take 21x the weight of the discriminative direction (u'Cu 0.0863 vs w'Cw 0.0035), and dropping the duplicate floor collapses C to isotropic noise (both forms drop to ~1/D). With both prunes on, though, the nuisance direction ends up weighted about the SAME as the discriminative one (0.0040 vs 0.0043), so the coloring is less selective than the hypothesis's "contributes exactly nothing" language implies.
solves_outside_model: Clean — nothing is solved outside the model. The target module's only inputs are z_obs (the batch's next-observation target embeddings) and pred; it never sees tok, command strings, cmds, window structure, depth, or the swap arm. It cannot parse a move chain because it is never handed one. At scoring time the only thing that runs is to_obs: one frozen global symmetric 768x768 matrix multiplied into the model's own prediction, bit-identical for every window, every candidate and both arms of the role swap, so it cannot inject resolved routing at the read and cannot move the paired difference by favouring an arm. C is estimated exclusively from the training split (harness._train's `fit`, which comes from M.split_train_dev(train_full)) — the cups windows are a different split, so there is no holdout contamination in the matrix either. This is a loss-geometry / readout-basis change, which is the legitimate side of the line; it is not the retracted stream-shape defect in a new axis.
summary: The estimator is implemented exactly as described and is leak-clean: unit-difference covariance of pruned k-NN pairs, trace 1, trace-renormalized, shrunk, float64 eigh, split into an exactly-inverse (C^{p/2}, C^{-p/2}) pair, identity until step 192, applied globally and frozen at scoring. I verified all of that by execution, including the two prune ablations the hypothesis says "are not decoration" (they are not). Two things diverge materially from the write-up. First, the map is NOT "identical for every step": it is rebuilt every 80 steps and each rebuild moves it ~11% in relative Frobenius norm with no decay out to step 992 — the model chases a moving target space for the entire run, a dynamic the hypothesis explicitly denies and never lists as a risk. Second, the crossover claims to keep the parent's transport head intact while changing "loss pressure, not a new input", but the transform breaks that head's basis: r2_dualaddress_move_transport injects raw-observation-space memory reads into the prediction through a DIAGONAL out_scale and additionally trains that same prediction against RAW observation candidates (pred_weight 0.5), while the objective now trains it toward fwd·z — and after 320 real training steps the prediction sits in the fwd space (||pred-fwd z||^2 = 2.84 vs ||pred-z||^2 = 34.9), with fwd carrying 26% of its energy off-diagonal, which no diagonal can follow. The arch's (D,D) readout could partly compensate, but the genome's optim caps its top singular value at 4.0 while fwd's top eigenvalue was 8.7 on my fixture. Three smaller things: the load-bearing premise "the loss charges prediction error uniformly across all 768 dimensions" is false for both r12 and r4 (both already apply an adaptive clamped per-dimension precision weight); "the condition number is single-digit with those settings" is a number the author could not have measured and my one realistic-fixture measurement contradicts it (11.8); and the argument that inv's amplification "is common to true and foil" is simply wrong — inv is applied to the prediction only, and the candidate bank is never mapped.

divergences.claim: "The map is one global matrix, identical for every step, every window, every candidate and both arms of the role swap" (hypothesis line ~92; repeated in DESCRIPTION: "identical for every step, every window and every candidate").
divergences.what_the_code_does: It is frozen and global AT SCORING (that half is true and is what makes the paired difference safe), but during TRAINING it is rebuilt every refresh_every=20 accums = every 80 steps from a momentum-0.97 EMA that never converges on batch-noisy estimates. I instrumented _rebuild_maps in a real harness._train run (1000 steps, bs=12, the repo's own eval/guard_reach structured board fixture) and logged the relative Frobenius change of fwd_map at each rebuild: 0.446 (first, from identity), then 0.129, 0.115, 0.108, 0.104, 0.090, 0.121, 0.116, 0.109, 0.117, 0.121 — ~11% per rebuild with no decay through step 992. The model is trained against a target space that keeps moving for the whole run; that is a training-dynamics property the hypothesis explicitly denies and never budgets for in its failure list.

divergences.claim: "From the parent I keep the two ROUTING mechanisms it already carries: … the head r2_dualaddress_move_transport (a dual-address delta-rule transport memory injected into the prediction)", and "Mechanistically the effect is a re-allocation of loss pressure, not a new input."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The target transform silently breaks the space the kept head operates in. r2_dualaddress_move_transport (a) injects the transport memory read into the prediction as `pred + rgate * (reads_t * out_scale)` where reads_t is built from RAW observation tokens and out_scale is a per-dimension (diagonal) parameter, and (b) its aux_loss scores that same prediction tensor (pred_weight=0.5) with an InfoNCE whose candidates and positives are the RAW observation embeddings `o` from tok. Once fwd != I the prediction must live in the fwd space, and it does: after 320 real training steps on the guard fixture, mean ||pred - fwd·z||^2 = 2.84 vs mean ||pred - z||^2 = 34.87. So the head's content injection arrives rotated relative to the space the loss lives in, and a diagonal out_scale cannot undo a map with 26% of its energy off-diagonal, while the head's pred-NCE actively pulls the prediction back toward the untransformed space. (The arch's injection goes through a learnable (D,D) readout and could compensate — except the genome's optim applies a spectral cap of 4.0 to (D,D) params, and fwd's top eigenvalue was 8.7 on the same fixture.) None of this is mentioned; the hypothesis presents the change as loss-geometry-only.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/head/r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py:150 `contrib = rgate * (reads_t * self.out_scale.view(1,1,-1))` and :306 `total + pred_weight * _nce(pred_cmd[b_idx, j_idx])` where `cand = o[b_idx]` are raw obs tokens; harness.py:104 adds head.aux_loss to the same loss. Measured in scratchpad/rev20/e2e.py (320 steps, bs=12): ||pred-fwd z||^2 2.84 / ||pred-z||^2 34.87; fwd eig range 0.742–8.735 (cond 11.8); off-diagonal energy fraction of fwd 0.26 (scratchpad/rev20/t1.py).

divergences.claim: "Both programs train with target = identity: the loss charges prediction error uniformly across all 768 observation dimensions." This premise carries the entire "WHY THIS SHOULD CHANGE THE MEASURED QUANTITY" argument.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Neither loss charges uniformly. Both r12 (parent) and r4 (the objective this candidate adopts) compute a detached per-dimension precision weight w = (1/(mse_d+eps))^0.5, normalized and clamped to [0.25, 4.0], and apply sqrt(w) to pred and tgt before every batch-wide distance. The baseline is already an adaptive DIAGONAL metric. Worse for the mechanism story: w is recomputed each step from residuals measured in the transformed space, so it partially counteracts the axis-aligned component of the new coloring (it cannot touch the off-diagonal component, which is where most of fwd's deviation lives). Only the raw_anchor (weight 0.05) and r4's relocation head are uniformly-weighted, and the relocation head is exactly the term r4's own DESCRIPTION says "works in the eval's own unweighted squared-L2 geometry" — which stops being true under this target.

divergences.claim: "I run p = 0.7 with shrinkage 0.1 because I cannot tune here and want the map's condition number bounded (with those settings it is single-digit)." Stated as fact; the author had no torch and could not have measured it.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The condition number is data-dependent: cond(fwd) = ((0.9·λmax + 0.1)/(0.9·λmin + 0.1))^0.35 after trace-normalizing C to mean eigenvalue 1, so single-digit requires C's top eigenvalue to stay under about 80 out of a trace of 768 (~10% of the unit-difference energy in one direction). On an idealized synthetic pair geometry I measured cond 4.36 (claim holds); on the repo's own structured guard_reach board fixture, in a real 320-step training run, I measured cond 11.77 with fwd eigenvalues 0.742–8.735 (claim fails). Neither fixture is the real encoder, so the claim is simply unestablished, not merely optimistic.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/rev20/t1.py: "fwd eig min/max 0.4979 2.1700 cond 4.358"; scratchpad/rev20/e2e.py (real harness, guard fixture): "fwd eig 0.7424 8.7353 cond 11.767".

divergences.claim: "The amplification inv applies to the model's output in low-contrast directions is harmless for the measurement by the same cancellation identity above — it is common to true and foil."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The stated reason is wrong. to_obs left-multiplies only the PREDICTION by inv; the candidate bank (true and foil) is never mapped (cups_probe._nway compares pred_obs against raw ctx["cands"]). Nothing cancels between true and foil, because inv touches neither. The decision variable is e·δ with e = inv·e_fwd, so the amplification does enter. The conclusion may still hold for a different reason (the amplified directions are the low-C ones, which are near-orthogonal to the confusable difference δ), but as written the justification does not follow from the identity it cites.
divergences.evidence: evolve/cups_probe.py:275 `pred_obs = target_mod.to_obs(pred, ctx["z_prev"])` then :143-149 `_nway` computes ((cands - pred_obs)**2).mean(-1).argmin() against untransformed candidates.

divergences.claim: "r4 is r12 plus command-orthogonalization plus a second head"; "Nothing in the parent's loss singles those rows out."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The second half is exactly right — r12 is loss(pred, tgt) with no WANTS_CTX, no trajectory segmentation and no relocation mining. The first half understates: on top of the cross-fit ridge nuisance shift and the relocation head, r4 also adds exact-duplicate multi-positive pooling, a class-size logit correction, row energy/inverse-class weighting and mean-relative temperatures. Direction correct, inventory incomplete.
